result_text:
I've finished the review and found one likely bug, in the new day-schedule code (`src/domain/day-timeline.ts`). Nothing else in the diff turned up a concrete failure.

```json
[
  {
    "id": "F1",
    "file": "src/domain/day-timeline.ts",
    "line": 124,
    "summary": "scheduleOf() can return entries out of time order, even though the design promises 'in time order'. It happens when a stop with no selected place has a set time earlier than the free time and drive before the next selected stop. TimelineBuilder.#addSelected pushes the free time and the drive first, then the waiting unselected stops, then the selected stop, so a waiting stop timed before the drive lands after it in the list. Fix: put each waiting stop with a known time where its time falls (for example, split the free time around it), or sort entries by start minute while keeping null-time entries in place. Otherwise, change the design's 'in time order' promise.",
    "failure_scenario": "Day: selected stop A ends at 4:35 p.m. Next is dinner, with no place yet and set for 5:00 p.m. (it holds the spot until 5:00). Then dessert, selected with a set time of 8:00 p.m. and a 20-minute drive. The entries come out as: A 3:35–4:35, free time 4:35–7:40, drive 7:40–8:00, dinner 5:00, dessert 8:00. Dinner at 5:00 is listed after the 7:40 drive, so a reader or the read_itinerary tool walking the list in order shows a schedule that goes back in time.",
    "severity": "nit"
  }
]
```

I ranked it a nit and not a blocker for two reasons. The design doc spells out this placement ("a stop with no selected place comes after the free time and drive"), and the bug only shows up when such a stop's set time is well before the next drive. The design's San Francisco example works because dinner's time matches the drive's arrival.

I didn't run the tests.

findings.summary: scheduleOf() can return entries out of time order, even though the design promises 'in time order'. It happens when a stop with no selected place has a set time earlier than the free time and drive before the next selected stop. TimelineBuilder.#addSelected pushes the free time and the drive first, then the waiting unselected stops, then the selected stop, so a waiting stop timed before the drive lands after it in the list. Fix: put each waiting stop with a known time where its time falls (for example, split the free time around it), or sort entries by start minute while keeping null-time entries in place. Otherwise, change the design's 'in time order' promise.
findings.failure_scenario: Day: selected stop A ends at 4:35 p.m. Next is dinner, with no place yet and set for 5:00 p.m. (it holds the spot until 5:00). Then dessert, selected with a set time of 8:00 p.m. and a 20-minute drive. The entries come out as: A 3:35–4:35, free time 4:35–7:40, drive 7:40–8:00, dinner 5:00, dessert 8:00. Dinner at 5:00 is listed after the 7:40 drive, so a reader or the read_itinerary tool walking the list in order shows a schedule that goes back in time.
